access.edition_or_version: Watts trans. Penguin 1999 (confirmed via Open Library)

mechanics.premise: A despairing prisoner is met by the allegorical figure of Philosophy, who diagnoses his illness and guides a graduated return of the sufferer's own reason rather than opening with argument or reproach (dossier section C).
tone_mechanisms_observed: presence-before-remedy: the consoler sits with the prisoner's sickness rather than correcting him (dossier section D)
diagnosis and graduated return: care begins with diagnosis of the illness and a gradual return of the sufferer's own reason, not with argument or reproach (dossier section C)
non-minimizing reframe: the loss is named before the larger frame (the impermanence of Fortune, the good), so the frame reads as perspective rather than dismissal (dossier sections C, D)
dialogic care: consolation staged as dialogue with an interlocutor (allegorical Reason), not as advice imposed from above (dossier sections C, E, F)
mechanics.point_of_view: Dialogic exchange between a despairing prisoner and the allegorical Reason who answers him (dossier sections C, E).
mechanics.emotional_progression: Despair met first, reframing last: acknowledgment and diagnosis precede any larger frame, so consolation never minimizes the loss (dossier section C).
mechanics.failure_or_misuse_signals: False consolation - telling the sufferer the loss does not matter - is the failure the tradition itself names; misapplied, the frame becomes 'everything happens for a reason' (dossier sections C, G).
mechanics.scope_note: Region is not stated in the dossier and is recorded as [] rather than inferred; no page, DOI, or quotation was added (dossier section F).
mechanics.verification_note: Latin text; Watts trans. Penguin 1999 confirmed via Open Library; technique described from the text's structure, not quoted (dossier section F).
